name: InputDeviceMonitor
src_typeComment: Tracks which KIND of input device the player most recently used — not a specific device, just "keyboard & mouse" vs "gamepad". This is what InputGlyphSwapper uses to decide which icon to show for a prompt like "Press [E] to interact" vs "Press [Y] to interact" — the swap happens automatically the instant the player's actual input changes, without you having to track it yourself anywhere.  A single shared static tracker rather than something each InputGlyphSwapper polls independently — a screen with a dozen prompt icons on it should still only be checking raw Input APIs once per frame, not once per icon.

src_members.sig: public static InputDeviceKind CurrentDevice { get; private set; } = InputDeviceKind.KeyboardMouse
src_members.name: CurrentDevice
EnsureRunning
src_members.comment: Called automatically by InputGlyphSwapper — you don't need to call this yourself unless you want the monitor running before any glyph icon exists (e.g. to read InputDeviceMonitor.CurrentDevice early).

src_members.name: ReportActivity
src_members.comment: Public rather than internal so both InputDeviceMonitorRunner AND a self-test (which lives in a separate Editor assembly) can call it directly — also handy if you ever want to force the current device from your own code (e.g. defaulting to Gamepad on console platforms).
